items: **The patch strands objects whose keys are too long for a request line.** `crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:2266` now refuses any bulk-delete `<Key>` over 1,024 bytes. The patch relies on single-object DELETE (`crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:1917`) as the way out for *every* over-limit object (the claims at `:493`, `:1818`, `:1978` and `crates/server/tests/s3_key_length_limit.rs:19`). That way out has a ceiling. The gateway runs on `axum::serve` with hyper defaults (`crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:279`). Hyper parses the request target with the `http` crate (`Cargo.lock:1608-1609`, 1.4.2), whose `Uri` rejects anything over 65,534 bytes, and hyper answers `414` before the gateway runs. **Concrete failing case:** seed `b/<'a' × 70,000>` through `Gateway::put_object`, as leg 4 does. On the patched code, HEAD is `414`, DELETE is `414`, bulk delete is `400 KeyTooLongError`, and the object is still present. On the pre-fix base, HEAD and DELETE are the same `414`s, but bulk delete answers `200` and the object is gone. Such keys can exist. `wyrd put --key` (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:562-568`) takes the key from argv (up to 128 KiB per argument on Linux) into the same metadata store. The CLI has no `delete` subcommand (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:415-416`), so S3 bulk delete was the only exit. Keys that need percent-encoding hit the ceiling sooner, at about 21,800 key bytes, because each byte becomes 3 wire bytes. Leg 4 seeds only a 1,025-byte key (`s3_key_length_limit.rs:319`), so it can't see this. Tagged `[human]` because the builder did what the brief said: criterion (3) demands the bulk refusal, while the invariant and C-1 demand that nothing becomes undeletable, and the two conflict above the URI ceiling. Options: drop the per-entry bound from bulk delete and keep the body cap; raise the bound above what a single DELETE can address; or accept the gap and record it (and/or apply the 1,024-byte limit to `wyrd put --key`, which the brief left out of scope).

Refusing the whole bulk-delete request (`crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:2270`, `:2114`) makes bucket-emptying tools fail on any batch that contains a legacy over-limit key. Concrete case, run as a probe against the patched tree: I seeded `b/<'a' × 1025>` through `Gateway::put_object` and PUT `k1`, `k2`, `k3`. ListObjectsV2 returns all 4 keys, including the long one. A `DeleteObjects` built from that listing answers `400 KeyTooLongError`, and `k1`, `k2` and `k3` all survive. Any client that lists keys and then deletes them in batches (`aws s3 rm --recursive`, `mc rm -r`, `rclone purge`) fails for every 1,000-key batch holding such a key, not just for that one key. The object itself is not stranded, because single-object `DELETE` still removes it (leg 4), so the brief's invariant holds as written. The patch does what criterion (3) asks. Whether whole-request refusal is the right design, or whether a per-key `KeyTooLongError` row (or no bound at all) would be better, is a brief-level call. This probably overlaps the round-1 finding already held for the human ("moot if the human drops the bulk bound").

**One stored over-limit key blocks bulk cleanup of up to 999 other keys.** `crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:2270` (with `:2114`) refuses a whole DeleteObjects (S3 bulk delete) request if any entry is over 1,024 bytes. Over-limit objects can still exist: those stored before this fix, or written with `wyrd put --key`. `list_container` lists them without filtering (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:714-741`). Concrete case:

**The deletion guarantee exceeds the deliberately retained limits.** `brief.md:33` promises “Bulk delete reaches every stored key, whatever its length,” and `brief.md:67-70` makes universal deletability an invariant, while `brief.md:112-113` excludes changing the 8 MiB body cap and request-target ceiling. On `$PDCA_TARGET`, `crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:507` sets that cap; `:1920-1921` rejects an overflowing body; and `:2007-2009` returns `400 MalformedXML` before deletion. The native fixture API adds no corresponding key-length check (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:235-256`, `:269-284`; `crates/core/src/metadata.rs:39-40`). A native-seeded `b/<a × 8,388,609>` needs at least 8,388,654 bytes in a one-key DeleteObjects body, so the retained handler refuses it; single-object DELETE also exceeds the brief's stated URI ceiling. The 70,000-byte fixture proves only a case below the body cap. This boundary is also explicit in the maintainer comment (`notes.json:1`): a single key is “bounded only by `MAX_DELETE_BODY_BYTES` (8 MiB).” Revise criterion (3), the invariant, and the planned documentation to promise preservation of existing deletion reachability, with no new 1,024-byte refusal, subject to existing request-format and size limits. Acknowledge the remaining recovery limitation alongside the native-limit deferral; retaining the universal promise would require additional scope beyond this PUT fix.
